advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Gate the echo pass (test 1) and the 'settle' pass (test 2) on `_wait_until_search_reflects` (or equivalent) confirming the just-pushed description content is search-visible before asserting `wrote_nothing_problem`, so index lag cannot be reported as an echo-safety regression.
evidence: The reconcile snapshot is built from search: `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py:410` ('the snapshot entries built from search_issues() above') and `fetcher.py:4`.

The module's own docstring acknowledges the hazard: test_dc_rich_text_live.py `_wait_until_search_reflects` docstring — 'The reconcile pass reads remote fields off a JQL search, and Jira's Lucene index is eventually consistent, so a field written a moment ago may not be visible to the pass yet.'

test_dc_rich_text_live.py:187-190 runs the echo `_run_bridge(... 'sync' ...)` with the comment 'the immediately-following pass must write nothing' and NO prior `_wait_until_search_reflects` on the pushed body.

test_dc_rich_text_live.py:230-235 similarly runs `settle` and asserts `wrote_nothing_problem(...) is None` right after `_push_and_converge`, again without a search-visibility wait for the landed baseline.
`_dc_support.py:249-276` (`wait_until_searchable`) documents the same eventual-consistency hazard reported 'in the worst direction' as an apparent bridge defect.
advisory.finding: The echo-safety pass (test 1) and the baseline 'settle' pass (test 2) run a reconcile immediately after an outbound push without waiting for the pushed description to become visible to the JQL search the pass reads from, so index lag can make the pass compute nonzero work and trip the zero-write assertion as a timing artefact rather than a real regression.
advisory.suggested_fix: After `_push_and_converge`, call `_wait_until_search_reflects` with a predicate confirming the pushed heading/bold/code token appears in the searched `fields.description` before running the echo/settle reconcile pass, mirroring the guard already used for the Jira-side edit.
